candidate.answerReason: The membership costs less exactly when 50+5x<10x, or x>10. The smallest whole-number visit count is 11.

methods.label: Compare total costs by an inequality
methods.explanation: The cost with a membership card is $50+5x$, and the cost without one is $10x$. Requiring $50+5x<10x$ gives $x>10$. When $x=10$, the two costs are equal, so at least 11 visits are needed.
methods.levelReason: Writing cost expressions and solving a linear inequality are within Grade 7 knowledge.

methods.label: Recover the fee through per-visit savings
methods.explanation: Membership saves \(10-5=5\) yuan per visit before accounting for the card fee. It takes \(50\div5=10\) visits for these savings to exactly cover the 50-yuan fee. Fewer visits leave the savings below the fee, and 10 visits only make the costs equal. One more visit makes membership cheaper, so the minimum is \(11\) visits.
methods.levelReason: This route uses elementary subtraction and division to explain the strict break-even threshold.
